description: German (de-DE) unit vocabulary, free-text unit mapping, rounding grid, piece weights and name conventions for Monsieur Cuisine ingredient lists, in the official style of the de-DE corpus.

allowedUnits.use: Everything that can be weighed, liquids included (water, milk, stock, cream, oil). 65.3 % of official rows.
Countable items that are not weighed: eggs, garlic cloves, herb stems, slices, bay leaves, whole lemons.
Spices, salt, baking powder, small amounts. Mixed case; TL appears 35 times.
Rare in official recipes; tablespoon amounts are converted to g in 88 % of cases.
Amounts above 1 (3 exceptions in the corpus).
Knife tip, with a dot (Msp without dot 13 times).
To-taste items: purpose suffix in the name, empty amount.

notAllowed: ml and l: 3 official rows in total; weigh liquids in g.
Household units in the unit field (Dose, Päckchen, Bund, Zehe, Scheibe, Tasse, Becher, Handvoll, Glas): map them as in freeTextMapping.

rules: A bare number as a string: integer (90.2 % of official rows), unicode fraction (4.8 %), empty (3.6 %), ASCII fraction (1.4 %).
No decimals for spoon amounts, no ranges, no units inside the amount field.
Fractions as unicode: ½, ¼, ¾, ⅛, 1 ½.
In step text official recipes put a space between number and unit: 500 g (official scale steps: 6996 with a space, 1 without; member recipes mix both styles).

grams.note: All 240 official amounts below 10 g are exactly 5 g; smaller amounts move to Tl, Prise or Msp.

roundingGrid.note: Bands are [from, to) in grams. Member recipes round less (below 10 g only 53 % on 5 g). Snap converted amounts to the grid; keep the user's amount when it is already on a coarser grid.
roundingGrid.spoons: Tl and El in whole, half or quarter units; Prise and Msp. in whole units.

freeTextMapping.note: 15 g is the default; weigh by food where it differs: seeds, poppy seeds, flour and starch about 10 g, ground nuts about 8 g, oil about 12 g, sugar and salt about 15 g, honey and syrup about 20 g
freeTextMapping.evidence: Member El rows with an official counterpart: g 88.2 %, Tl 7.6 %, El 2.3 %. 15 g per El from only 7 stated weights; liquids and powders differ (oil about 12 g, flour about 10 g, honey about 20 g).

freeTextMapping.alternative: g for amounts of 5 g or more of sugar, butter or oil
freeTextMapping.evidence: Member TL rows: official Tl 55.9 %, g 32.9 %, Prisen 7.9 %. 5 g per Tl from 9 stated weights.

freeTextMapping.alternative: Tl for salt in savory dishes (official gives salt in Tl: Prise rows map to Tl in 65.3 %)

freeTextMapping.target: Stück when the item is not weighed by a scale step, otherwise g
freeTextMapping.evidence: Member Stück rows: official Stück 52.2 %, g 31.5 %, empty 15.8 %. Median stated piece weight 80 g over 979 annotations.

freeTextMapping.nameRule: write the clove into the name: Knoblauchzehen (290 official rows, plural even for 1)
name ends in 'aus der Dose/Glas' (202 official rows)
name ends in 'aus der Dose/Glas'; take the drained or net weight from the source

freeTextMapping.evidence: 9 stated weights, spread 50-300 g: low confidence

freeTextMapping.nameRule: write the stem into the name: Petersilienstiele, Thymianstiele (327 official rows)
name ends in 'in Scheiben' (35 official rows with Stück, 7 with g)

freeTextMapping.evidence: 2 stated weights: low confidence; use the package size from the source

freeTextMapping.note: no stated weight in the corpus; estimate and add a review hint

US cup; not in the corpus. 240 ml × density holds for liquids only; for solids use: flour about 125 g, sugar about 200 g, rice about 185 g, grated hard cheese about 90 g, whole cherry tomatoes about 150 g per cup.

pieceWeights.note: Grams per piece or package from weights stated in the corpus ("1 Zwiebel (80 g)", scale steps, "à 170 g" in names). Entries with at least 4 observations.

nameConventions: Use the catalog spelling: 99.2 % of official rows link a catalog id; ids and names map one to one.
Counted items use the plural catalog name even for 1: Knoblauchzehen, Eier (Größe M).
Qualifiers go in parentheses (fat content, egg size, flour type: 17.5 % of official names) or after a comma (schwarz, gemahlen, getrocknet: 26 %).
To-taste items: purpose suffix in the name and an empty amount, for example 'Salz zum Abschmecken' (210 rows) or 'Mehl zum Verarbeiten' (81). 96.8 % of official 'zum ...' rows have no amount.
Optional markers (n. B., nach Belieben, etwas) are a member habit (12.1 % of member rows have one); official recipes almost never mark items optional.
Equipment listed as an ingredient (jars, baking paper, moulds) goes into a ZUBEHÖR group and never counts toward the bowl mass (348 corpus rows).

groups.style: Upper case (99.6 %): FÜR DEN/DIE/DAS <component> (56 %), yield header such as FÜR 12 STÜCKE (31 %), AUSSERDEM (8 %), ZUBEHÖR (4 %).

perPortionMedians.note: Median amount per portion over recipes counted in Portionen; a sanity check for scaled amounts.

servings.default: 4 Portionen (750 of 2221 recipes; median 4 for Portionen recipes)

corpus.note: Generated by npm run corpus:build-knowledge from the corpus of this locale: unit spellings, group names and serving units of official recipes, with counts. Evidence for the hand-written vocabulary, not read by the converter.
